Title: tournament report : Walk through Arcadia (Paris - sept. 8th 2007)

Messages.Author: Stone
Messages.Body:
Tournament name : Walk through Arcadia (sanctioned, multijudge, co-organized
by Sebastien Rouillard, Prince of Paris, and myself ; 3round+1 final with 2h
time limit)
Where : Paris, shop Troll2Jeux
When : september 8th, 2007
Dudes : 19 players

Finals : Orian (Julio Martinez) -> Kamel (Setite Venenation/M1KF) -> Nikolaj
(Prince with potence) -> Margaux (Malk 94) -> meh (weenie animalism)
Margaux basically rapes me with heavy bleeds (it took 1h due to help from
Orian and Nikolaj), but her vamps are either low on blood or in torpor, so
Nikolaj easily ousts her with bleeds for 1 some 15min later. He didn't have
any predator, as Kamel had been in blood doll/hunt mode the whole time (he
was scared of heavy bleeds from Julio Martinez and other !Nos with dominate
and was rather clearly going for 2nd place anyway).
Then the final gets kinda boring, as Orian and Kamel are struggling for 2nd
place. Kamel had tried to deal a 2/2/1 with Nikolaj, but Nikolaj didn't
really go forward after ousting Margaux, having secured 1st place anyway (he
was top seed or something and there wasn't going to be enough time to get to
'one man standing'). So he simply gained pool with blood doll/hunt, while
Kamel was cycling useless actions (bleed/mask/majesty etc.) to fetch
deflections. Orian ousted Kamel a few seconds before the time limit.
Final rank : 1/ Nikolaj (1.5VP) 2/ Orian (1.5VP) 3/ Margaux (1VP) 4/ Kamel
(0VP) 5/ meh (0VP)

Finalists get 4-6 boosters and 6 promo cards ; each non-finalist got 1 3rd
Ed. booster and 6 promo cards (Victor Pelletier, Angelo etc.)
As a side note, this tournament was the first for Orian's girlfriend,
Sabrina who got her very first VP in first round.
Additional note from the Prince : since this tournament was organized more
or less on the fly (basically an unsanctioned tournament was cancelled so we
took the opportunity to use this schedule slot), so it should be entered
properly on WW's site after the NAC or something (in other words, it's not
possible to check for results at the moment, for TWD).

Congrats to Nikolak for his victory.
Thanks to the players for an overall friendly tournament ; to the multijudge
volunteers (Orian, Margaux, Reyda, Mumra, Killerbee, Ankha) and thanks to
Troll2Jeux for their hospitality, as always.

Messages.Author: niko...@hotmail.com
Messages.Body:


Thanks for a nice tournament, Stone.

I made the deck a couple of days before, and hadnt had a chance to
test it. I posted it here (there is a discussion somewhere here) and
the general idea was that it wouldnt work. I still thought the idea
would work out, so decided to try it either way.

1st round.

Me, daughters with arts traumatic essence, ishtarri bleed/vote,
lasombra bleed, old school group 1 princes.

It wuickly became clear that this was an optimal table for me. No
combat decks, and a prey/pred with only light stealth. I was able to
torporize a couple of my preys minions while bloating so I had 4
princes. My predator couldnt pass his votes and I blocked the few
bleeds he attempted.
When he was a 5 pool, he was bleed for 5 at 2 stealth (couldnt be
pushed higher) and was about to deflect to me. I told him to deflect
it to my prey instead, who was at 6 pool, and then I would let him
have two points in the end. After a lot of talking he did that, and I
ousted my prey the following turn. My new prey had spent alot of
energy on getting the lasombra really low (a delayed Elders command
undeath can be pretty expensive). I was going slowly forward with my 5
princes and bleeding for 4-5 each round. My predator decided to trust
me fully and threw 2-3 KRCs at my prey and helped me oust both of
them.
When it was down to the two of us, I decided to break the deal. I had
an almost 100% chance of getting a sweep here and decided to go with
it. My seating here was optimal, and I didnt expect to do as well at
the other tables, where I assumed there would be some gun decks and
some weenie ani (which destroys this deck).
1 GW, 5 VP for me (and ended up with 6 princes on the table).

2. round (4 player table).

Me, weenie pot starring lorrie, anti tremere black hand, ishtarri
bleed/vote (from round 1).

I had the choice of influencing out cock robin or jaroslav, and since
I knew my prey had a lot of sabbat POT guys in his crypt, and since I
would need the extra intercept vs the bleed/vote pred, I went with
Jaroslav. My grand prey saw that it was a weenit pot deck and
influenced for the first many rounds so he could bring out 3 vamps at
the same time. When he did, he was down to 6-7 pool and desperately
needed help.
I started out with no combat in my hand at all (which is quite amasing
considering the number of them in the deck) and had to keep low until
I could build a good hand. It did cost my grandprey dearly and he was
eventually ousted. I did manage to torporize lorrie with a torn and
decap, which slowed him down, but not enough. After that the pot and
ishtarri decided to oust me first, and then fight it out.

Fortunately I was able to block almost all his actions, and parity 4-5
times to get pool back for the actions I had to let through, while
defending against the rushes from my prey. I managed to get them both
so low, that my prey had to oust my predator for fear of getting
ousted himself.
I had 7 princes and he had 5-6 potence guys. It was looking good until
a crazy round where 4 of my princes went to torpor and a fame was
played on Spiridonas. I ran out of cards on the following turn, but
due to sacrificing spiridonas in a block and getting him torporized
(taking me down to three pool)

My prey was at two pool.. I had three cards in my hand and only donal
on the table there was a tension, so I bleed with him, played my torn
signpost and immortal grapple and my prey lost a pool to his own
Tension in the ranks, Donal went to torpor, I had one card left in my
hand and no ready vampires, and my prey died in his untap phase due to
the fame.
It was a cool ending.. :)

2 VP (and 7 princes on the table, although all in torpor.. hehe)

3. round

Me, malk anti bleed, anneke, maris/rachel parity deck, pot/pre/obf
vote/bleed deck.

My grandpred started out with 2 or 3 zillahs and then went into Parity
"mode". I allowed some two of them in return for pool, seeing as my
pred minion tapped back to 15 pool, but couldnt stop the later ones
due to a legendary vampire. My prey was bleeding forward and
eventually ousted anneke. The legendary vampire was removed and when
the fourth prince hit the table I had the vote lock. Then I used a
couple of parities to hurt my prey and keep my predator alive. I
ousted my prey with bleeds and parities, and a bit after that my
predator died to the bleeds from his predator. I was relatively
secure, with 5 princes out at the time. We went forth and back a bit
with more parities, but he played no combat cards at all, so any block
he or I made meant a malk in torpor.
I brought out Spiridonas and my prey laughed a bit. I thought he
remebered the special of Spiridonas, but when he later let the bleed
through and I burned all the blood on spiridonas, then he told me that
he forgot about it.. :)

1 GW, 3 VP

So I went into the final first seed with 2 GW, 10 VP.

I only knew that Stone was playing weenie ani, that Kamel was playing
some sort of settite and that Margaux played some sort of malk.
I didnt know what Orian played, so I decided to sit between the two I
expected didnt have any intercept.

Margaux started bleeding right away quite heavily ("Ozmo bleeds for
6"), while I was building up. Kamel was afraid of his predator and
just wanted to bloat and didnt think he could get through me. I got
out my four initial Princes while trying to keep Stone alive with
parities and Orian kept him alive with DIs. I actually wanted Stone to
get ousted, as I would lose princes fast to weenie ani combat, but I
wanted Margaux to be so weak that I could oust her right after. I
managed to get it into a position where Margaux went all out, taking
her only vamp Mariel down to 0 blood in the attempt of getting
through. I had a DI I could use on the last stealth, but decided not
to, and Stone was ousted.
My prey was a 10 pool, with Mariel out with no blood and a blood doll,
and then transfered out Roland.

After that I bled with my 5 princes while keeping the three second
trads in my hand in case Kamel wanted to get sneaky (I was allowing
him to bloat to stay alive, and let bleeds for one through to remove
the edge from my prey. Margaux was ousted a few rounds afterwards and
due to the seeding I was winning at that moment. The amount of talk in
the final meant that I had no way of ousting Orian, so I just secured
my position and bloated. Kamel was ousted in the last minute and I won
with 1,5 VP.

The final was indeed not very interesting to watch. It is the second
final I have played here in Paris, and the other one also timed out
(with no one getting ousted at all).
The paris crew is cool to play with, but they really do talk too
much.. :)
I think my turns combined must have lasted between 10-15 minutes of
the final (I'd say roughly 8-10 turns). The rest was spent on the hour
long discussions about very small details and deals. I think everyone
should try to play with the Danish crew at last once in their life.
More playing there, and less talking! hehe.

(And the argument that deals are needed in order to ensure that games
actually end isnt really true. I have never played a final in Denmark
that actualyl timed out (or that many games for that matter). I think
people should trust in the attrition based mechanics that are in the
game already, and just get on with the game. The talk can definitely
be limited, and it would actually mean that more games come to a
conclusion).

Again, thanks for a cool tournament to Stone and the judges, and I'll
hopefully see (and oust) you in the French Championship.

Nikolaj

"# 4.8 Made "play to win" explicit. Added explanation of handling
deals vs. play to win, and added DIRECTIVE TO IGNORE DEALS WHEN ONLY
TWO PLAYERS REMAIN

4.8. Play to Win
One aspect of sportsmanlike conduct is that players must not play
toward goals that conflict with the goal of the game as stated in the
V:TES rulebook (e.g., attacking certain players on the basis of their
V:EKN ratings or overall tournament standing, etc.). For tournaments,
playing to win means playing to get a Game Win if it is reasonably
possible, and when a Game Win is not reasonably possible, then playing
to get as many Victory Points as possible.

Neither the basic game rules nor the tournament rules enforce or
regulate deals made between players. The tournament rules acknowledge
deals, however, in that a deal which represents the best interests of
the players involved at the time the deal is made is allowed to be
honored, even when the normal play to win rule would indicate that a
deal should be broken. This only applies to deal that are in the best
interests of the players involved at the time the deal is made. That
is, it applies only when making the deal is playing to win. (It is
also allowable to break such a deal, of course).

Exception: when only two Methuselahs remain, the tournament rules no
longer acknowledge any deals. PRIOR DEALS ARE VOIDED, even if they
were play to win when made. When only two Methuselahs remain, both
Methuselahs must play to win based only on game state, WITHOUT REGARD
TO ANY DEALS."

There can be no decision to break a deal that has been voided. Any
recognition of a voided deal is a violation of V:KEN 4.8.



"Exception: when only two Methuselahs remain, the tournament rules no

At the time when the deal was made, my predator was looking at getting
ousted the same turn, or the following turn at the latest. Therefore
getting 0 VPs.

The offer I gave him would let him get 2 VP.

Our argument is that if, when its down to 2 players, if one player has
3 VPs he has won already, no matter the outcome of the endgame.
As you quote above, both Methuselahs must play to win. The player with
3 VP has already won the game and therefore follows the rule above,
the player with 2 VPs cannot win the game.

The assumption here, and I guess this is where we need an official
clarification, is that the "play to win" still follows the "get as
many VPs as possible" in the respect that when you cannot get any more
VPs (or if you either cannot win or you have won already), then you
can choose to get those VPs (or choose to win or lose) in whatever way
you choose.

So we both believed that I had the option of upholding the deal, and
that is obviously what my predator believed I would.

That is how it has been played, at least here in Paris, since the
introduction of those rules. I have been against VP deals all together
up until this tournament, where I decided to see how big a difference
it makes to how I play, so I am not the most experienced in the
intrigate system of VP deals. (I am just very convincing).

> Actually, isn't a 3-2 VP with a concession at the end still possible
> under the proposed rules?

As I understand it no, it is not still possible. By definition, you
can not concede a game and still be declared the winner. Conceding,
in this definition, would be to yield the game win to the opposing
player. This can not occur as the player yielding has 3 VP's and by
rules must play for the game win.

You don't concede victory points. You concede a game win.



Messages.Author: XZealot
Messages.Body:


Yes, it explains the mechanics of a table agreeing to concede.

Conceding is an agreement between players that one player should gain
all the victory points left on the table.

All deals are at their foundation nothing more than agreements between
players.

Deals are not enforcable under the rules.

V:EKN 4.8 specifies that all deals are voided in the end game.

A player who is in a winning position with 3 VPs is not allowed to
concede the game to a player with 0 VPs as it is an agreement to give
another player 2 VPs, and all deals are voided when there are only two
players left.

Therefore, there can be no conceding in a two player game.

In the big discussion that came from the VP deal issue, Stone didnt
reply to this, but I'll try to explain it. :)

Kamel didnt sit down thinking "Hmm, I think I'll go for second place
today. I dont want to win another tournament.". But he knows his deck
(he told me afterwards that he has about 12 stealth cards in his deck,
6 of which are mask of a thousand faces, and therefore had little to
no chance to pass me if I should have a second trad in my hand. He saw
from watching earlier games that I play alot (14), and therefore had
two choices.
a) He bets everything and tries to go forward, with a high chance of
getting blocked and torporized, as his only defense was majesties,
after which the DOM pred could bleed him out easily.
b) He tries to convince me that I should take the 3 points, which he
will help me do, and then I leave him 2 VPs in the end. Thereby
maximising both his VPs and his final position. He was seeded 4th into
the final afaik.

Also, his allies were in no position to help him, as his grandprey was
going full throttle forward trying to oust her prey, and his
grandpredator very fast went to 4 pool with only a 4 and a 5 cap
vampire out.

So, it was a similar deal to the one that lead to all the other
discussion, and since that has been deemed to be in correspondance
with the rules (although I agree that for the game in a grander
scheme, it does suck), in my eyes he did what he had to do. Or if
nothing else, what he felt he had to do.

I hope that explains it better than " and was rather clearly going for
2nd place anyway". :)

Nikolaj
